title: Relative Hom algebraic spaces from finite locally free scheme sources
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:Z\to T$ be a finite locally free morphism of $S$-schemes [def-pc-finite-locally-free], allowing variable rank and rank zero. Regard schemes as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Let $X$ be any algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], equipped with a morphism $f:X\to T$. Define the functor $H_{Z,X/T}$ on $S$-schemes by
$$H_{Z,X/T}(U)=\{(a,b)\mid a:U\to T,\ b:U\times_{a,T}Z\to X,\ f\circ b=a\circ\operatorname{pr}_U\}.$$
Here fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and restriction along $v:V\to U$ sends $(a,b)$ to $(a\circ v,b\circ(v\times_T\operatorname{id}_Z))$. There is an algebraic space $H$ over $T$ and a natural isomorphism of its functor of points with $H_{Z,X/T}$, under which the structural map to $T$ sends $(a,b)$ to $a$. No separation, quasi-compactness, flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05Y7 (proposition-hom-functor-algebraic-space), specialized to scheme Z and T; the functor is equation-hom-functor, Tag 05Y2, in its equivalent description immediately before that equation.

proof.text: Write $H_X=H_{Z,X/T}$. It is an fppf sheaf. Indeed, an fppf covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Compatible pairs $(a_i,b_i)$ have a unique glued map $a:U\to T$ by [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf], viewing $T$ as an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. The base-changed family $Z_U\times_UU_i\to Z_U$ is fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Apply the same morphism-gluing statement with target $X$ to obtain the unique $b:Z_U\to X$. The equation $fb=a\operatorname{pr}_U$ holds because it holds on this covering and maps to $T$ are unique there. Thus the pair glues uniquely, including on the empty test scheme.

source.place: Tag 05Y3, lemma-hom-functor-sheaf, first proof paragraph; scheme-source specialization.

proof.text: For every $U\to T$, $p_U:Z_U\to U$ is again finite locally free: finiteness is [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), flatness is [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and local finite presentation is [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). These are exactly the three conditions in [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. In particular no constant positive rank has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 05Y7, first paragraph; Tag 02KD expanded into the existing permanence statements.

proof.text: Choose an affine open cover $\{T_\lambda\}$ on which $Z\to T$ has finite free coordinate algebra. To justify this without a constant-rank hypothesis, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant] first gives the open-and-closed rank pieces $T_d$. Cover each $T_d$ by affine opens; their inverse images in $Z$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b) and remain finite locally free of degree $d$. Apply [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-principal-basis-cover] to each resulting affine morphism and refine by its principal opens. This yields the required finite bases, with $d=0$ permitted.

source.place: Tag 05Y7, first paragraph: choice of finite-free affine base charts.

proof.text: For any $T'\to T$, put $Z'=Z\times_TT'$ and $X'=X\times_TT'$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives a natural identification $H_{Z',X'/T'}=h_{T'}\times_{h_T}H_X$: its section on $U$ is $(c:U\to T',b:Z_U\to X)$ with $fb=(U\to T'\to T)\operatorname{pr}_U$. The inverse sends $b$ to $(b,c\operatorname{pr}_U)$ as a map to $X'$. Both maps commute with restriction because their two projections do. Thus the restrictions to the preceding base charts are precisely the Hom functors for their base-changed data. It remains to prove algebraicity over each finite-free affine chart; we do this in Steps 5–10.

For any representable surjective etale $Y\to X$ over $T$, consider $H_Y\to H_X$ by postcomposition. Over a scheme test $(a,b)\in H_X(U)$ set $W=Z_U\times_{b,X}Y$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $W\to Z_U$ is surjective etale. A lift of $b$ over $V\to U$ is exactly a section of $W_V\to (Z_U)_V$: send a lift $c$ to $(\operatorname{id},c)$; conversely project a section to $Y$. These operations are inverse and commute with pullback. By [lem-sfb-etale-sections-finite-locally-free], this test fibre product is an algebraic space etale over $U$. By [lem-sfb-finite-etale-cover-local-sections] it has a section after a surjective etale $U'\to U$, so its map to $U$ is surjective. This proves exactly the scheme-test etale-surjective comparison required below, without using algebraicity of $H_X$.

source.place: Tag 05Y5, lemma-etale-covering-hom-functor: explicit identification with Tags 05XR and 05XQ.

proof.text: Now assume $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ finite free over $R$. First take $Y=\coprod_{i\in I}Y_i$ with each $Y_i$ affine. For a finite subset $E\subset I$, let $Y_E=\coprod_{i\in E}Y_i$ and $F_E=H_{Z,Y_E/T}$. The finite coproduct $Y_E$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], including $E=\varnothing$. Thus [lem-sfb-affine-finite-free-hom] represents $F_E$ by an affine scheme over $T$. Regard these as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 05Y7, third paragraph, application of Tag 05Y6 to finite target unions.

proof.text: The inclusion $F_E\subset H_Y$ is representable by open immersions. For a test $(a,b)$ on $U$, let $C=b^{-1}(Y\setminus Y_E)$, a closed subset of $Z_U$, since $Y_E$ is open and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Set $U_E=U\setminus p_U(C)$, open by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. For $v:V\to U$, the pulled-back map lands in $Y_E$ exactly when $Z_V\times_{Z_U}C$ is empty, equivalently when $v(V)$ misses $p_U(C)$. Indeed a nonempty fibre of $C$ over a point remains nonempty under its residue-field extension: choose a vector-space basis containing $1$ in one field extension; after tensoring with the other, the resulting free module has a nonempty basis, so the tensor ring is nonzero and has a prime. Hence this condition is exactly factorization through $U_E$. Factorization of a morphism into an open subscheme is unique by restriction of the underlying map and sheaf map. Consequently the test fibre product is $h_{U_E}$.

source.place: Tag 05Y7, third paragraph: the open-immersion assertion, with the finite-image locus written out.

proof.text: These open subfunctors cover $H_Y$. It suffices to lift sections over affine tests $U$. Then $Z_U$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The open subsets $b^{-1}(Y_i)$ cover $Z_U$; quasi-compactness supplies finitely many of them, so $b$ factors through some $Y_E$. Over general $U$ apply this on an affine open cover, giving local lifts, exactly sheaf surjectivity. The finite subsets of $I$ form a small set in the same universe. The affine representing schemes of $F_E$ can all be chosen there: the polynomial presentation in Tag 05Y6 uses only the coordinate rings of $T,Z,Y_E$, a finite basis and subsets of these rings. Their scheme coproduct therefore lies in the chosen big site by [def-weil-size-convention, lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The coproduct of the $F_E$ is algebraic by [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct], using their identity atlases. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-space-open-gluing] to conclude that $H_Y$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 05Y7, third paragraph, covering and gluing, including its size footnote.

proof.text: For arbitrary $X$ over this affine chart, choose a surjective etale atlas $Y\to X$ with $Y$ a disjoint union of affines by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Step 8 makes $D=H_Y$ an algebraic space. Step 5 gives for every scheme test of $H_X$ an algebraic-space pullback $D\times_{H_X}h_U$ which is surjective etale over $U$. Etale maps are flat and locally of finite presentation on etale charts by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The fppf sheaf property is Step 1. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] hold with source $D$ and target sheaf $H_X$; this proves algebraicity on each finite-free affine base chart. There is no separation or finiteness condition on $X\to T$ in this argument.

source.place: Tag 05Y7, second paragraph and Tag 04S6, after the disjoint-affine-target case.

proof.text: Return to arbitrary $T$. Step 4 identifies $h_{T_\lambda}\times_{h_T}H_X$ with the functors now proved algebraic. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-local-algebraic-space] over $T$ to the affine open cover from Step 3. Its chart-size hypothesis holds: the cover and its finite-basis refinements are small, the constructions in Steps 6–9 stay in the universes fixed by [def-weil-size-convention], and the coproduct of the chosen scheme atlases exists there by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. This gives an algebraic space $H$ over $T$. Its identification with $H_X$ is the sheaf identification throughout; the structure transformation $(a,b)\mapsto a$ is a morphism to $h_T$ because restriction sends $a$ to $a\circ v$. Therefore it gives exactly the asserted functor of points and structural map.

source.place: Tag 05Y7, first paragraph, local algebraicity and its descent back to the original base.
